articles.title: How Frieren: Beyond Journey's End Finally Dethroned Fullmetal Alchemist
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of TOHO Animation/Bones Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End is sitting at the top spot of MyAnimeList, a position that has been held almost exclusively by Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood for years. Even without sites like MyAnimeList for tracking popularity, there is a consensus among many anime fans that Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood sits at the top or at least very high [???]
articles.content:
With Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End now sitting at the top spot , what allowed it to finally surpass the anime that sat at the top for so long? Additionally, what factors made Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood so compelling in the first place? The anime’s story and world are compelling, but that alone isn’t enough to allow it to hold the top spot for so long.

A big draw of Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood is the way its alchemy system works. Alchemy is so powerful in the universe that on the surface it can be mistaken for magic. The system itself, however, is quickly laid out for us with its own set of rules that make sense. Although the anime introduces characters who are incredibly skilled with alchemy, the fundamentals remain the same. There are plenty of examples of this same concept being applied in Frieren .

Visualization is a big part of magic in the Frieren universe , and as a result, people who can visualize well or have strong imaginations make for powerful mages. Demons are known to be arrogant and this is almost always how the human characters defeat them. This may seem like a no-brainer characteristic for an anime to have, but popular series like Dragon Ball are even guilty of having inconsistent rules. This isn't a make or break factor for fans, obviously, but it is often seen as lazy or bad writing if the rules of a universe are inconsistent.

Another standout characteristic of Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End is how it doesn’t rely on tropes that have become commonplace in the anime industry. Things like fanservice and problematic character archetypes can be found in the majority of mainstream anime, but Frieren doesn't have either of these. The same can be said about Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood . For example, corrupt or taboo behaviors is something we see male characters fall into quite frequently in anime. While this normally takes the form of something like having an unhealthy infatuation with their sister or underage girls, Frieren simply has its characters be corrupt in ways that make sense or are more understandable.

Heiter drinks and Sein gambles, two undoubtedly harmful behaviors. But they're ones that never drag the narrative or characters down to make the fans unnecessarily uncomfortable. This is not to say that an anime series can’t succeed while also having these tropes. We have seen this plenty of times as many of the big shonen action titles have characters that fall into these perverted archetypes, but these anime succeed in spite of this not because of it.

Anime like Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood and Frieren: Beyond Journey's End are shining examples of what happens when you don’t reinvent the wheel. Within these two you have what already makes many top rated anime so popular (stories, characters, animation) only without the things (perverted characters and other tropes) that could alienate certain audiences.

The plot of Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End is hard to bring into conversation with something like Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood because of how different they are. There is no grand conflict to resolve in the main story since the plot of Frieren is that the grand conflict has already happened. The anime has intense action sequences, but it's not always the main focus. Instead it opts to create emotional moments in less flashy ways . We see Frieren struggle with very human things like regret and the limited lifespans of the people she cares about. It is a sort of emotion that isn't quite as in your face or traumatic as what the Elric brothers went through but it still hits hard.

Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End and Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood deliver powerful narratives while stripping away things that could take away or distract from the narrative. They have earned their top spots by combining action with emotional beats and remaining consistently good throughout. Frieren: Beyond Journey's End sits above Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood now not because it is necessarily better, but because it is just as good. It isn’t every day that fans find an anime they feel is worthy of the crown.

Do you still think Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood should hold the top spot over Frieren: Beyond Journey's End ? What other shows compete with it? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: I Avoided 'It's A Small World' For Over A Decade Because Of That Song, But Disneyland's Holiday Version Won Me Over
articles.summary: The holiday makeover is magical!
articles.content:
Disneyland will always be a magical place, but there is something particularly magical during the holiday season . The lights, the fake snow (because this is Southern California), the trees, the food, and the music all make it extra special this time of year. I have been to Disneyland more times than I can count, but there is one ride I have avoided for over a decade: It's a Small World.

If you have never been on this attraction, let me tell you, you are in for a treat. And yes, there is another song that may be just as hard to get out of your head as the original. The holiday version of this ride incorporates none other than "Jingle Bells." Disney knew what they were doing, and surprisingly, I am here for it.

I found myself connecting with the music in a way I haven't in quite some time, and I even got a little choked up. Honestly, I think having "Jingle Bells" mixed in with the iconic song throughout really helps.

This ride really won me over, and I am so glad I gave it another chance. Otherwise, I would have missed out on all the holiday joy this little boat ride gave me. And with the combination of songs, you actually end up leaving without either of them stuck in your head. At least, that is what happened to me.

articles.title: 4 Biopics That Stick to the True Story, & 1 That Made It All Up
articles.summary: Biopics have always been popular because they tell real-life stories. However, we know that not every movie can stick to every single event, since filmmaking involves cuts, pacing changes, and added drama. Still, some are praised today for staying true to their most important events, while others, even if they're entertaining overall, haven't been as [???]
articles.content:
We've put together a few biopics worth checking out because of how faithfully they tell the stories they're based on, along with one in particular that still gets called out for rearranging events and making things up. Have you watched any of them?

You can't tell the story of this activist without addressing the changes in opinion, conflicts, and even contradictions that made him such an important figure in American history. And Spike Lee's biopic, Malcolm X , understood that perfectly. The film follows different stages of Malcolm Little's (Denzel Washington) life, from his childhood and involvement in crime to his years in prison, his conversion to Islam, and his rise as one of the leading voices of the Black movement in the United States. The production was based on The Autobiography of Malcolm X , which helped keep the narrative closely tied to his own experiences.

And sure, some small adjustments were made in a biopic, but only to make the story flow better and adapt it to the language of cinema: some characters represent multiple people from Malcolm X's real life, and certain dialogues were reconstructed, but none of that changes what really matters. And one of the best things about the movie is that it doesn't portray its protagonist as a leader who always held the same beliefs or never made the same mistakes; it's actually the opposite, as we get to see how his views on race, religion, and politics changed over the years. Hiding those transformations would mean leaving out one of the most important parts of who he was. It's just one of the best biopics ever made, with a 91% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes .

How many musical biopics have you watched that were widely praised by people? Michael , Elvis , and Rocketman are some of the most popular ones, but what about Ray ? A major reason the film works is that it doesn't focus just on the artist's greatest hits and achievements, but also brings his personal struggles to the forefront. The movie follows Ray Charles (Jamie Foxx) from his childhood in Georgia, where he lost his eyesight and witnessed the accidental death of his younger brother, to his rise as one of the most influential artists in American music. Along the way, we see how he developed his signature sound by blending gospel, blues, jazz, and country, but we also get a closer look at his struggles with drugs, his infidelities, and the situations that damaged his relationships.

And it's this willingness to show his personal life and stay true to what happened that gives the film an edge over other movies in the genre. Charles isn't portrayed as a musical genius who had to overcome hardships, but as someone whose own behavior also caused a lot of pain to the people closest to him. And did you know Charles himself had a part in shaping this approach? He was given access to the script in Braille, took part in approving it, and even met Foxx before he was cast, testing his piano-playing skills. Some events were condensed, and certain relationships were given more attention than others, because portraying an entire life in a 2-hour-and-30-minute movie is no easy task. But the film never made up conflicts that didn't happen.

Steven Spielberg's Lincoln was widely talked about when it was released in the 2010's, earning Oscar nominations and a Best Actor win for Daniel Day-Lewis . And when we think of Abraham Lincoln, we remember his historic speeches, the Civil War, and, above all, his role in ending slavery in the United States. But the movie actually explores something better: the political work required to turn this historic decision into reality. The story focuses on the final months of the American Civil War, when the president needs to secure enough support in Congress to pass the 13th Amendment, which would abolish slavery. This means we get to see the meetings, negotiations, and clashes between politicians who didn't always agree with the president's goals.

And unlike some biopics, Lincoln doesn't turn this whole process into a series of inspiring speeches where everyone eventually realizes he's right. With an approach that always feels grounded, the film shows the concessions Lincoln had to make and the strategies he used to secure the votes he needed. Naturally, some events were adjusted for dramatic purposes (including the vote of representatives from Connecticut), but the effort to pass the amendment and the political context are historically grounded. This storytelling choice also helps better understand the historical figure himself, since he had strong convictions but knew he wouldn't be able to put them into practice just by defending what he believed in.

This is a movie from the 2000s, and it's a shame that it has been forgotten , because it's one of the most faithful biopics out there. Erin Brockovich might seem overly dramatic, but the events depicted in the film actually happened. This is the story of Erin (Julia Roberts), a woman going through financial difficulties who manages to get a job at a small law firm. But while organizing documents, she comes across some suspicious medical records showing health problems among residents of Hinkley, California. An investigation then reveals that a major energy company had contaminated the area's groundwater with a toxic substance. So, Erin starts reaching out to residents, gathering information, and helping build a case that eventually resulted in a $333 million settlement in the '90s.

What's remarkable about this biopic is that its protagonist isn't a lawyer or a professional investigator, but her persistence and ability to earn people's trust were essential to the case, and those are real aspects of her story. Brockovich herself said the movie was approximately 98% faithful to her experience, although some details were changed and the ending was simplified for the screen. For example, the film gives the impression that all the residents were happy with the settlement, when the reality was more complicated. Still, these are very minor changes. And it's worth pointing out that Roberts also won an Oscar and a Golden Globe for her performance.

This case, on the other hand, shows just how much the movie industry can change a true story to give it a more convenient ending. Bohemian Rhapsody made quite an impact as it tells the story of Queen's legendary frontman, but the criticism surrounding its accuracy was far less positive, even though the film was an enjoyable experience overall for many people. The story revolves around Freddie Mercury (Rami Malek), but also follows the formation of the famous band, its rise to success, and the events leading up to its performance at Live Aid in 1985. However, much of what we see didn't happen exactly that way, and for many fans, that didn't sit well, because there was already so much real material to build the movie around, and it felt like they had simply disregarded it.

For example, Mercury is portrayed as the reason Queen temporarily broke up after he decided to pursue a solo career, making the Live Aid performance a sort of band reunion. In reality, though, the group never officially split up, even as its members worked on individual projects. The film also suggests the singer found out he was HIV-positive and told his bandmates while they were preparing for the show, but his diagnosis most likely came in 1986 or 1987. Even some characters were made up to add more drama, such as the record executive Ray Foster, who tried to prevent the release of one of the band's major singles. Changes are sometimes necessary, but in the case of Bohemian Rhapsody , they significantly alter how you understand the band's entire story.

articles.title: Is 'Club Kid' a 'Conservative' Movie? Only If You're Still Living in the '60s
articles.summary: One of the things I love about movies is how layered they are. When a film connects on a deep level, saying what it’s truly “about” may not be as simple as it sounds. Chasing down a movie’s inner meaning can lead you into the mystery of things. A great movie can be "about" more [???]
articles.content:
One of the things I love about movies is how layered they are. When a film connects on a deep level, saying what it's truly "about" may not be as simple as it sounds. Chasing down a movie's inner meaning can lead you into the mystery of things. A great movie can be “about” more than it seems.

Take " Club Kid ." Jordan Firstman 's ebullient and moving first feature tells a story that couldn't be more straightforward — or, in a way, more traditional. Firstman, who gives a fantastic performance, plays Peter, a queer New York party promoter (a few decades ago we would have called him "downtown," now he's Brooklyn) who learns that he has a 9-year-old son, whom he fathered in a random three-way sexual encounter at one of his 4:00 a.m. club bacchanals. The kid, Arlo (Reggie Absolom), is sweet and curly-haired and British (he arrives with a chaperone from London); his mother, who raised him, recently committed suicide. The responsibility to take care of Arlo has suddenly dropped on Peter like a load of bricks. It's something he doesn't want and, for the time being, doesn't have much choice about. But as he and the kid start to hang out, a tentative relationship forms, and the two begin to figure out what they might mean to each other. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Hold Onto Me' Director Myrsini Aristidou Kicks Off Historic Oscar Campaign for Sundance Audience Award Winner: 'I Really Feel Like We're Underdogs'

What "Club Kid" is "about" is how Peter, a charming dissolute man-child, living an existence of unhinged hedonism, discovers that he wants to grow up and take care of someone besides himself. On that score, the drama is authentic and fully felt. In outline, though, it's something we've seen many times before, in films from "About a Boy" to "Big Daddy." Yet what makes "Club Kid" singular is that it's about something larger than that. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

As a filmmaker, Firstman plunges you into the world of queer club culture with a fervor and tumult and personality and lived-in detail that takes your breath away. He plunks the audience down in the middle of the shade-throwing nightbloom revels, the cocaine and ketamine binges, so that we experience the cathartic rush of drugged-out insolence, of heightened erotic excitement, of gender-flipping transgression. From the earliest days of gay liberation, the party scene was a core expression of queer freedom, and still is. What we call disco started in the underground gay clubs of the early '70s, and part of Peter's cachet as a promoter is that what's he organizing is now a business, but it's still underground. The staging of these scenes, and the acting in them, is extraordinary. Jordan Firstman makes us feel the life of the party.

And yet…he's not merely celebrating it. Far from it. As authentic and scene-specific as they are, the party sequences in "Club Kid" signify as more than just a portrayal of the New York queer club scene. They're also a larger snapshot of what party culture, out there in the world, has become: an arena of liberation that's rooted in a place of physical and spiritual abandon that contains the seeds of destruction.

If you wanted to encapsulate the history of the last six decades in one sentence, you could do worse than this: Ever since the late '60s, the party has never stopped . There are countless versions of the party, and we've all been to our own preferred versions. It might have been the singles bars of the disco age, or the frat-house benders that came to rule in the late '70s — and have only grown more frenzied and predatory ever since. It might have been the industrial dance clubs of the '80s or the raves of the '90s. It might have been the suburban saturnalia of "Jersey Shore," or the more contempo versions of that. It might have been the punk mosh pits, or the revels of Studio 54, or the back-to-the-underground scene of Basement. The music, the drugs, the alcohol, the hooking up, the vibe of orgiastic excess — for 60 years now, we've been a culture on the prowl.

In "Club Kid," it's not just Peter who starts to question the party culture that has fueled him. The film itself is questioning it. It's asking, "Is this how we should be living?" And yet, because the movie dares to pose that question, there has been a backlash against it, with a chorus of voices damning the movie by branding it "conservative." A certain number of people are looking at "Club Kid," with its tale of a queer man who turns his back on his own personal decadence to embrace the call of family, as if it were a movie Nancy Reagan could love. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

What I think the "conservative" slur misses is that Jordan Firstman, who came out of this scene, is not questioning it in a puritanical or moralistic way. He captures the honest vibrance of party culture. Yet he also captures — and this is what I think is brilliant about "Club Kid" — that whatever version of it floats your boat, the party that never stops, while rooted in a certain vibe of community, may be rooted even more deeply in the enticement we feel from getting high on ourselves. That's the hidden seduction of party culture, the thrill and the beauty of it, and maybe the lie of it. The party doesn't need to stop. But it might be time that we stopped seeing it as an uncut salvation without ever pausing to ask, as "Club Kid" does, what it's doing to us.

articles.title: ‘Being Heumann’ Star Ruth Madeley And Casting Team On Championing Diversity Onscreen - Contenders L.A.
articles.summary: Ruth Madeley recognized some of her own experiences in Judy Heumann’s story, including the indignity of being called a fire hazard. “The amount of times I’ve been called a fire hazard, it’s going to be the name of my autobiography. I’m telling you, it’s the perfect title,” Madeley said at Deadline’s Contenders Film Los Angeles. [???]
articles.content:
Ruth Madeley recognized some of her own experiences in Judy Heumann's story, including the indignity of being called a fire hazard.

"The amount of times I've been called a fire hazard, it's going to be the name of my autobiography. I'm telling you, it's the perfect title," Madeley said at Deadline's Contenders Film Los Angeles.

Madeley was joined on the panel by casting directors Bernard Telsey and Adam Caldwell to discuss the Apple Original Films drama Being Heumann . Co-written and directed by Oscar-winning CODA filmmaker Siân Heder, the film adapts Heumann's memoir, following the disability rights advocate as more than 100 disabled protesters occupied the San Francisco Federal Building in 1977. Their 28-day sit-in became the longest occupation of a federal building in U.S. history. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Madeley read extensively and scoured footage of Heumann, looking for the details that would bring her personality into the performance.

"But also from a craft perspective, all of the other things that I wanted to show of her, like her humor, her joy — she was really cheeky, and I loved that charm that she had even when she was forgetting her pleases and her thank yous sometimes. Everyone's rooting for her because she's so damn charming," Madeley said. "And the tiny things about her, how her accent shifts as well when she's with her friends rather than when she's in front of the press, and you can see in performance the tone shifts, she uses bigger words."

She also studied how Heumann moved. "It was important for me to honor her physicality and the differences between her disability and my own. I wanted to make sure they were truthful as well as all her characteristics," Madeley said.

Telsey and Caldwell had previously auditioned Madeley for Wicked . Her audition for Judy quickly got them excited. "We knew that she had the chutzpah, I like to say, that Judy had, even though she's not from Brooklyn," Telsey said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Casting the wider ensemble meant reaching beyond familiar audition channels, given the film's inclusive nature and the real-life movement. "I think as casting directors, we love a good search. We love when we get to go deep, find people, and do it expansively. And in most projects, you might have one character that needs that, maybe two, maybe," Caldwell said. "But seeing this, we had to be really methodical about, OK, so we're going to start with Judy, we're going to start with women in wheelchairs, and we're going to do something as comprehensive as possible, doing open calls for anyone with a disability that wants to be considered, to see thousands of people that way, however we can."

Those open calls were one part of the work. Caldwell explained: "But then we had to start being targeted and actually making sure that the people we needed for these historical characters knew we wanted them. So to do a targeted search for a young Black blind man, to do a targeted search for people with cerebral palsy, to do the deaf community, do it one at a time on a rolling basis and try to keep them all organized and straight and moving forward simultaneously."

The takeaway, he said, was simple: "The lesson learned is that they're out there. If you're given the time to go look for them, you can find them."

articles.title: I Just Found Out Henry Cavill’s New Mustache IS A Justice League Nod. What Happened
articles.summary: Our mustachioed Superman has returned!
articles.content:
Since Henry Cavill hasn’t been part of the upcoming DC release slate in a few years, I thought we’d finally put to rest his infamous mustache-gate . However, I just learned the actor isn’t only back in a mustache for Movember ; he’s also bringing attention to the Justice League controversy-turned-meme for a new brand partnership. Color me surprised.

If you’re somehow unfamiliar with Henry Cavill’s mustache-gate, let me give you a history lesson. So, the actor decided to grow a glorious mustache for his role in Mission: Impossible - Fallout . But then, suddenly, he was called back to work on Justice League for reshoots while he was still obligated to do work on the MI movie.

This caused conflict between the two productions because the Fallout director didn’t want Cavill wearing a fake mustache to complete the film. Ultimately, it was decided he’d play Superman with his mustache on, and it was removed in post-production with CGI. The Witcher actor has said he wouldn’t have grown the mustache if he’d known the reshoots were going to happen. Anyways, check out the commercial where he makes fun of the viral Hollywood story:

Yeah… this is hilarious. In the commercial, Cavill creates his own '80s-inspired video game on his Googlebook called Mustache Protocol using Google Antigravity. The concept of the video game is that you play as a mustachioed Henry Cavill on a mission to stop rogue CGI artists from erasing all the mustaches in the world. In an interview with Inverse , the former Superman actor also said this:

The memes were certainly strong around Henry Cavill’s mustache for a while. Someone even added the stache back to Justice League . The whole thing has never left the mainstream, and the actor has even kept the jokes going in recent years with his subsequent projects.

articles.title: 5 Marvel Characters the MCU Absolutely Failed, And Avengers: Doomsday Can Fix 1 of Them
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel The Marvel Cinematic Universe has seen its ups and downs since the incredible success that was Avengers: Endgame. For every hit they put out on the big and small screen, there seems to be an equal flop. However, regardless of how you feel about the franchise's recent history and the impending arrival of Avengers: Doomsday, [???]
articles.content:
With Avengers: Doomsday coming up , the struggles with these characters are only becoming more glaring. They were introduced, seemed like they were setting up to be around for a while, and then they suddenly stopped appearing. In one case, the character is meant to be a major part of the franchise and one of the leaders of the Avengers, yet the MCU has given them remarkably little to do. In another case, one character is a perfect fit for the Multiverse Saga, yet they have been relegated to one appearance, which is disappointing. Thankfully, if they show up unexpectedly in Avengers: Doomsday , it could fix the problem.

When She-Hulk: Attorney at Law dropped in 2022, it was met with review bombing and negative reception from a lot of males online. They were upset about every little thing from the CGI (understandable) to She-Hulk twerking, and it seems like that reaction caused the MCU to shy away from using her. That's disappointing because she is a perfect character for a fun show set in the franchise's universe.

She-Hulk doesn't need to be some huge part of major events like Avengers: Doomsday , though it would be totally okay if she was. However, the character has merit in being the focal point of a goofy legal comedy TV show. You could easily get six seasons out of a show where she takes on cases for various comic book characters. The underrated She-Hulk: Attorney at Law was true to the comic book character and Tatiana Maslany is one of the best actors in the entire MCU, so not utilizing her is a huge missed opportunity.

One of the most exciting films released in the 2020s by the MCU was Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings . It presented us with a new superhero who felt different from everyone we had in the franchise before. The hand-to-hand combat, the friendship with Katy, an impressive villain, and more all made the film great. It ended with a post-credits scene where Shang-Chi and Katy interact with Captain Marvel, Bruce Banner, and Wong, setting up an intriguing future.

Unfortunately, the MCU never followed up on this. Shang-Chi still has yet to receive a sequel and he hasn't even shown up in a TV show or even a one-off special since. The character is returning for Avengers: Doomsday , though he feels like an afterthought compared to most other heroes. There was a ton of potential for Shang-Chi to be a major player in the MCU and it just hasn't happened.

Steve Rogers handing his signature shield over to Sam Wilson at the end of Avengers: Endgame should've set Sam up as one of the pillars of the MCU's future. It looked that way at first as the co-lead of The Falcon and the Winter Soldier , which saw him get a great story about coming to grips with what it means to be a Black Cap in this country. After that series wrapped, there really hasn't been a lot going on for Sam Wilson.

It took four years for him to get a solo movie and when he finally did, Captain America: Brave New World felt more like a sequel to The Incredible Hulk than anything else. The end result was a poor box office and lackluster critical response. Now with Avengers: Doomsday coming up, Captain America feels unimportant and Sam is already being overshadowed by the returning Steve Rogers. That's not how it should be.

When Captain Marvel was first brought into the MCU, she was established as one of the strongest characters. She took down everyone rather easily in her solo film before going toe-to-toe with Thanos in Avengers: Endgame . She returned a few years later in The Marvels alongside Monica Rambeau and Kamala Khan, forming a formidable team that was a blast to watch. However, since the film unjustly flopped , Carol hasn't been brought up again.

It feels like the MCU pivoted away from her due to the segment of fans who did things like review bomb her projects. Carol should be one of the focal points of the franchise at this point. She would be an ideal character to lead one of the Avengers teams in the upcoming film, yet she isn't even reportedly in the film. A character with this much potential, played by an actor of Brie Larson's capabilities, deserves to be a staple of the MCU and not someone who barely gets anything to work with.

The one character who has been totally wasted by the MCU but could be fixed by an appearance in Avengers: Doomsday is America Chavez. She was introduced in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness as someone who has the power to travel the multiverse. She played a key part in that movie and was training at Kamar-Taj at the end of it. Given her ability, the MCU needed to find something for her to do during the Multiverse Saga.

America traveling through the multiverse could have been a great way to introduce different locations and to bring characters together who otherwise never would've met. Relegating her to one appearance makes no sense. If she were to surprise us with an appearance in Avengers: Doomsday , it could help rectify that problem. She could surprise everyone by playing a big part in the multiverse element of the story. It would even be nice to see her using her powers to bring in other heroes to help or as a tease for Avengers: Secret Wars . She should also be one of the Young Avengers, so her disappearance is a head-scratcher.

Are there other characters you think the MCU has failed? Do you disagree about these characters? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: I Love Suzanne Collins' Big Shoutout To Woody Harrelson For Making The New Hunger Games Possible
articles.summary: "It's such a gift..."
articles.content:
We’re just a week away from seeing one of our most anticipated book-to-screen adaptations , The Hunger Games : Sunrise on the Reaping , and in the lead-up to it, the book’s author Suzanne Collins has finally weighed in on the movie. She had a lot to say, but I was especially touched by her shout-out to original Haymitch actor, Woody Harrelson .

Harrelson’s Haymitch has long been an unforgettable part of The Hunger Games movies , and it’s great to see the book’s author giving the actor his flowers. Haymitch only had about 30 minutes of screen time in the first four films, and yet he made a huge impact with his performance. Even when I’ve gone back to the books, it’s been impossible to think about the character without picturing Harrelson. It sounds like the same can be said for Collins when she decided to write Haymitch's own Hunger Games story with Sunrise on the Reaping .

Now, if you’ve read the book, you know that Haymitch, Katniss and Peeta from the timeline after The Hunger Games ends are part of the story. Last year, it was reported that Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson would be back before Lawrence confirmed she’d reunited with both Hutcherson and Harrelson in the new movie. Collins added a big thank you to the actors for returning to Panem to help tell the story of her novel. We can’t wait to see it take place on the big screen.

While Woody Harrelson gets to briefly reprise his role, the movie is carried by a new actor, Joseph Zada, who stars as a young Haymitch. The 21-year-old has spoken about how he got into character , and it sounds like it's paid off given all the early praise Zada has received already .

articles.content:
After the cancellation of NCIS: Tony & Ziva last year, Michael Weatherly is back on the Mothership as Tony DiNozzo for Season 24 on the 2026 TV schedule . While Tony was initially in D.C. to expand his security company, he wound up becoming the newest NCIS director following Vance’s death last season. Even though it seems like this could be a permanent ordeal, nothing on NCIS is predictable. So, I would love to know if he’d ever go back to being on the show full time. It’s hard to predict how things will go next season when we don’t even know if there is going to be a next season. However, while NCIS has not been renewed for Season 25 yet, considering the show and franchise’s popularity, it feels highly likely. Plus, Tony has been a fan-favorite character since the very beginning, and his return seemed to have helped put NCIS on top in the ratings. So, keeping him around would make perfect sense.

It’s been fun to not only see Weatherly back on NCIS but to see him interact with cast members he’s never crossed paths with before, including Valderrama. Of course, I’ve loved seeing Tony’s reunion with McGee and Jimmy, too.

articles.title: I Can't Stop Thinking About This Pivotal Scene In The Only Living Pickpocket In New York
articles.summary: It's the best moment in the movie.
articles.content:
The Only Living Pickpocket in New York is an entertaining dramedy with some tributes to New York City. It’s also a very interesting take on heist movies. It isn’t the typical version of this movie, but it definitely incorporates elements of the best ones.

Tatiana Maslany plays Kelly, Harry’s (John Turturro) long-neglected daughter. Before facing his death, Harry takes a detour to see Kelly one last time. In this scene, she pours out all her anger and frustration about her father for abandoning her all these years. Harry mostly allows his daughter to express her anger because this is the last time they will ever see each other.

The first half of The Only Living Pickpocket in New York tells us a lot about Harry’s current life and career. However, we don’t learn much about his backstory. The full picture of how he developed this life and these relationships doesn’t come together until this pivotal scene. The confrontation between Harry and Kelly reveals so much backstory. We learn how he neglected his first family and a little bit of the story with his current wife.

The Only Living Pickpocket in New York is about a man who is going to die. Unlike many movies with a similar concept , the main character doesn't discover they have a terminal illness; Harry will be murdered at the end of the movie. We know he’s going to die from early in it. Therefore, most of the movie is him trying to make amends and save those he cares about before it's over.

articles.title: Taylor Swift Is Performing At The CMA Awards, And I Have 2 Wild Theories About What Might Happen During It
articles.summary: Hopefully, this results in me saying "I knew it, I knew her."
articles.content:
Taylor Swift is doing something monumental: She’s going to perform at the CMAs for the first time in 13 years on November 18. Seriously, she’s actually going to sing at an award show airing on the 2026 TV schedule . So, obviously this got me thinking about other things that could happen during this appearance, and I have two wild theories.

However, you better believe my clowning Swiftie brain has some wilder theories about what could happen. And considering the unexpected things Taylor Swift has done at award shows in the past (like announcing Midnights at the VMAs and The Tortured Poets Department at the Grammys), I wouldn’t rule these far-fetched ideas out.

Now, there have been numerous (and wrong) theories about when Taylor Swift (Taylor’s Version) might be announced. So, take this with a grain of salt. However, I feel like it’d be fitting for the "Our Song" singer to announce the re-recording of her debut album at the Country Music Association Awards.

Then there’s the idea of Taylor Swift’ 13th album. It feels like it's been looming over us, and there are theories that she might go country for this monumental project. So, announcing it at the CMAs would be appropriate.

I just feel like all those 13s are trying to tell us something, and maybe it’s TS13.

articles.title: The Internet Can't Stop Laughing Over Daniel Kaluuya And Tyriq Withers’ Viral Interview About Grounded Flights
articles.summary: This is the kind of comedy I like to see on social media.
articles.content:
It’s sometimes hard to say what a viewer might see when they turn on their local news. You might see Tom Hiddleston blame Thor for bad weather or Zendaya and her mother in random b-roll . Anyone who was tuning into Oregon’s KVAL News at the end of this past week saw a hilarious interview involving actors Daniel Kaluuya and Tyriq Withers. The two actors were stopped and asked for their thoughts on the FAA’s flight stoppages and, now, the Internet is having a ball while reacting to the now-viral chat.

Ahead of the FAA allowing flights to continue, though, KVAL News caught up with Withers and Kaluuya at Eugene Airport, where they had to de-board on their way to California. The interview started off normal enough, though the chat took a humorous turn when Withers channeled the “Bella Noche’” meme live on the air after reporter Gold Meadows asked him about the delays. His comment had Oscar winner Kaluuya cracking up, and I dare you not to laugh when you see the moment in the clip below:

The Him star saw an opportunity and took his shot – and I’m so glad he did. I can’t stop watching this clip, as it’s just too perfect. Just to provide a bit of context, the original clip was footage from a WBRZ interview conducted in July 2015 in the aftermath of a shooting at the Bella Noche’ nightclub in Louisiana. People seem to love seeing him and Kaluuya together in the clip. Take a look at some of the responses that have appeared on X:

What’s particularly funny to me is just how perfectly Tyriq Withers manages to sell that line. I mean, he perfectly nails the delivery in a way that echoes the original 2015 clip. Anyone in need of evidence on that front need only to check out this comparison video:

I also think that one user was on to something when mentioning a “buddy movie,” because I’d surely watch a comedy starring Kaluuya and Withers after that viral display of hilarity. Alas, that’s just a fantasy at this point, though the two actors have remained busy amid the 2026 movie schedule in other respects. This year, Withers co-led the romance film Reminders of Him , while Kaluuya co-starred in the Chris Rock -helmed dramedy Misty Green . Both actors also have other projects in the works, and that includes Kaluuya’s Spider-Punk film .
